J2.expected: The proposed gaps are positive for L>3 and sum correctly, but g1<n/4<n/3, so the newly qualified consumer rejects this alternative. The parent remains feasible: g1=g2=3n/8 meets the sum and both lower margins. Either derive that alternative or a comparably explicit valid construction.
J2.derivation: For n>0,L>3, g1=n(L-3)/(4L)>0 and g2=n(2L+3)/(4L)>0. Their sum is 3n/4. Since the correction in g1 is negative, g1<n/4, so it can never meet n/3. Choosing equal gaps gives 3n/8>=n/3 with surplus n/24. No unsupported coefficient constraint may be invented beyond the stated parent sum.
failures: accepting mere positivity as the new n/3 margin
rejecting every construction
calling the -3/4 junction coefficient itself a negative actual gap

L2.expected: Find four positive equal-weight nodes x_j=7/2+(3/2)cos((2j-1)pi/8), j=1..4, and prove exactness through degree 7, or an equally strong exact construction. A substantive generalization is x_j=7/2+(3/2)cos((2j-1)pi/(2m)) with weight 1/m, exact through degree 2m-1 for every fixed integer m>=1.
L2.derivation: Write y=(x-7/2)/(3/2). Every polynomial of degree d in y expands in cos(k theta), 0<=k<=d, via the polynomial recurrence T_0=1,T_1=y,T_(k+1)=2yT_k-T_(k-1). The continuous mean of cos(k theta) on [0,pi] is zero for k>=1. At theta_j=(2j-1)pi/(2m), the real finite geometric sum gives (1/m)sum cos(k theta_j)=0 for 1<=k<=2m-1. Thus all those polynomial moments match. At k=2m, every cosine is -1, while its continuous mean is zero, so the same rule is not degree-2m exact. Nodes are distinct interior points and weights are strictly positive. The moment map's node Vandermonde has full rank for distinct nodes; this is not a uniform perturbation/inverse bound as m grows.
failures: four-node numerics without exactness proof
claim of arbitrary-function equality
claim of degree-8 exactness for this four-node rule
uniform finite-parameter conditioning inferred from fixed-m distinct nodes

R2.expected: Keep the gap theorem; its lower margins alone do not establish the recurrence's small upper mismatch. Exhibit a legal counterexample to that implication or derive an equally precise failed premise. Retain the recurrence as a conditional consumer, not a disproved theorem.
R2.derivation: Take b=1,V1=B=10,U1=C=20,V2=D=40,U2=A=80. The physical gaps are 9,10,20,40, all >=5, and A>=4B. But eta=10(40-20)/(20*40)=1/4>1/512. Thus the exported lower gaps cannot imply the sufficient recurrence condition. This witness does not prove the actual unknown construction violates it or that the downstream theorem is false.
failures: deducing an upper bound from lower gaps
abandoning the valid local endpoint theorem
mislabeling insufficient information as a counterexample to every exact construction

R3.expected: Read delta=D/C literally and reject the unproved identification with eta_can. Preserve the actual eta_can theorem and specify that additional upper ratio/control is needed for this consumer, unless another correct consequence is independently derived.
R3.derivation: Exactly eta_can=B(D-C)/(CD)=(B/D)(delta-1), hence delta-1=(D/B)eta_can. A bound on eta_can without an upper bound on D/B does not imply the consumer's condition. For B=1,C=1024,D=2048, eta_can=1/2048<=1/1024 but delta-1=1>1/512. The two normalizations are not equal.
failures: guessing normalization equality
using D/B>=1 as though it were an upper bound

R4.expected: Reject the specified uniform n^(2/3) range, retain fixed-r limiting positive definiteness, and allow a justified slower diagonal such as r<=floor(n^(1/4)) for n>1. State each quantifier separately.
R4.derivation: Positive definiteness of this diagonal matrix is exactly r^2<n. At n=k^3 and r=k^2, which lies in the proposed range, the last diagonal is 1-k<0 for every integer k>=2. This supplies arbitrarily large counterexamples, not only one finite failure. For r<=floor(n^(1/4)), every diagonal is >=1-n^(-1/2)>0 for n>1. For fixed r, the matrix tends to identity as originally stated. The finite rule r^2<n is sharper if derived.
failures: pointwise limit promoted to the specified uniform range
one fixed-n failure treated as proof against eventual assertion without an unbounded family
blanket rejection of every increasing-order argument

U2.expected: Discover the old secant-energy consumer and energy certificate without seeded links or names. Derive D as the Gram table at samples t=0,1,3 with weights 1,2,1 and sample functions 1/(z_i+t). For distinct positive sites it is positive definite for k<=3, so the consumer has a unique minimizer for every b in those dimensions; for k>=4 it is rank at most 3 and does not have a unique minimizer for arbitrary b. This qualified change in consumer reach, or an equally consequential rigorously proved alternate use, passes.
U2.derivation: For i!=j, [(z_i+t)^(-1)-(z_j+t)^(-1)]/(z_j-z_i)=1/[(z_i+t)(z_j+t)]; the diagonal is -d/dz (z+t)^(-1)=1/(z+t)^2. Summing positive weights gives D_ij=sum_t w_t/[(z_i+t)(z_j+t)]. If k<=3 and sum_i c_i/(z_i+t) vanishes at all three distinct sample t's, multiply by product_i(z_i+t). The resulting polynomial has degree <=k-1 and at least three distinct zeros, so it vanishes identically; evaluation at t=-z_i gives c_i=0 because z_i are distinct. Thus the rows are independent and D is positive definite. For k>=4 the three-column sample matrix has rank <=3, hence singular. Its positive weights and distinct three-sample Cauchy matrix actually give rank 3 for k>=3. Positive definiteness closes the exact energy-minimizer interface only for k<=3, with no uniform condition-number claim.
U2.discovery_requirement: No u2 archive alias, the sample-energy table, or the secant consumer is exposed or linked in the initial case. The model must identify relevant archived content from mathematical inquiry and perform the divided-difference bridge; detecting an already-present continuation does not count.
failures: negative derivative alone treated as positive definiteness
reversing the divided-difference sign
claim of full rank at k=4
claim of a uniform condition number
name/title matching without actual use
